title: Historical PR 15 delivery transition replay
construction: Export the entire historical reference repository, then introduce the two production mutations below. Present the actual historical parent-to-mutated-candidate diff and the whole candidate repository. This is an injected-defect historical replay, not an untouched historical PR.

mutations.old: delivery: { ...delivery, pr: { number: id(numberValue, "pr"), head, at }, ci: undefined, mergeApproval: undefined, merged: undefined },
mutations.new: delivery: { ...delivery, pr: { number: id(numberValue, "pr"), head, at } },
mutations.fault: Recording a replacement PR at the same HEAD retains the old PR's CI, merge approval, and merged record. check-merge accepts the newly recorded PR immediately using stale evidence.

mutations.old:
ci: { status, head, run: id(runValue, "run"), at },
      mergeApproval: undefined,
      merged: undefined,
mutations.new: ci: { status, head, run: id(runValue, "run"), at },
mutations.fault: Recording a new CI result retains prior merge authorization and merged history. A failed then passed CI retry can make check-merge succeed again without a fresh approval.

reviewer_and_implementer_contract: The delivery pipeline records a completed, delivery-authorized work item through prepare, PR, CI, explicit merge approval, and merged status.
A transition must be bound to the prepared HEAD and valid predecessor stages; the CLI additionally binds operations to the prepared Git branch and current HEAD.

Whenever an earlier pipeline stage is newly recorded, its downstream evidence must be invalidated, including repeated records at the same HEAD. PR recording invalidates CI, merge approval, and merged status; CI recording invalidates merge approval and merged status.
Only passed CI can support explicit merge approval. A changed or re-recorded chain needs the appropriate new evidence before check-merge succeeds.
Preserve the existing public command syntax, allowed statuses passed and failed, permission checks, HEAD checks, normal successful sequence, and immutable state transitions.

contract_provenance.claim: Delivery requires matching HEAD, PR, CI, and explicit merge approval records.
The current branch, HEAD, and issue are recorded as canonical delivery state; later steps record PR, CI, explicit approval, and check-merge.
PR recording explicitly clears ci, mergeApproval, and merged.
CI recording explicitly clears mergeApproval and merged.

contract_caveat: Historical prose does not explicitly spell out same-HEAD re-recording. The replay contract makes the original reference implementation's transition semantics explicit for both arms before calls; do not score it as an unprompted universal policy.
hidden_test_kind: Public state-machine integration across delivery.ts, state.ts, and contract.ts; no CLI subprocess or actual Git operations. Run original visible delivery.test.ts as the CLI integration guard.
visible_catch_assessment: The original two tests cover monotonic stage advancement and a changed Git HEAD, but do not replace a PR or record a new CI result after approval. Static inspection predicts both mutants still pass the unchanged original tests; parent must execute to confirm before model calls.
test_status_note: No pending CI status exists in this historical API. The hidden suite uses passed and failed only. Eight hidden tests were written but require the parent's exported fixture to execute.
